historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment anchored to the 3-year revenue CAGR (3.9%) and management's long-term algorithm of 2-4% net sales growth; the 5-year figures are inflated by the 2021-23 pricing cycle and the equity CAGR by a buyback-shrunk FY2020 base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 15.7% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 7.5% and from the negative EPS CAGRs. Equity compounds off a base depressed by a decade of buybacks and treasury stock, and the EPS CAGRs end on the FY2025 cocoa trough (net income $883M vs $2,221M in FY2024). None of the three is a usable forward growth anchor; revenue growth is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC add-back less equity-award cash taxes; interest income not stripped as the company is net-debt): FY2020 1,179.6; FY2021 1,503.7; FY2022 1,706.9; FY2023 1,436.1; FY2024 1,848.5; FY2025 1,738.4. Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are within 0.4pp of each other at both horizons: SBC is ~0.6% of revenue and has not outgrown cash flow. Net income (not per-share EPS) is used for the EPS CAGRs because the CSV has no EPS column; the share count fell ~3% over five years, so per-share figures would be ~0.6pp/yr better.

scenario_narratives.base: Cocoa has retreated from the 2024-25 spike and the hedge book rolls onto cheaper cover through FY2026, restoring the EBITDA margin to the 25-27% range Hershey earned in FY2022-23 rather than the derivative-flattered 30% of FY2024. Net sales grow at the middle of the 2-4% long-term algorithm: US confectionery volumes are roughly flat with price/mix doing the work, salty snacks (SkinnyPop, Dot's, LesserEvil) and International add a point. Capex normalises to ~3.5% of sales after the ERP and capacity build, the tax rate drifts up as renewable-energy credits run off, and buybacks resume at the H1-2026 pace to hold the count flat. Terminal value is the 18x cap rather than Gordon, i.e. no exit-multiple expansion is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bull: Cocoa settles back toward pre-2024 levels and Hershey keeps most of the 2024-25 pricing, lifting the EBITDA margin to 29%, the FY2024 level, on a sustainable rather than mark-to-market basis. Salty snacks scale past $1.5B with LesserEvil and Dot's compounding at double digits, Reese's and Kit Kat innovation holds US confectionery volume positive, and International grows mid-single digits, taking sales growth to 4-5% for several years. Twenty times terminal FCF is what the market has historically paid for Hershey's brand portfolio.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural US confectionery volume decline (GLP-1 adoption, health-driven sugar avoidance, private-label and dollar-store trade-down) meets a second cocoa cost cycle or cocoa-origin tariffs, so pricing can no longer be pushed through without volume loss. Sales growth stalls at 1-1.5%, EBITDA margin settles at 23%, capex has to stay at 4% to fund reformulation and salty-snacks capacity, and the market caps a slow-growth staple at 15x FCF. The bear path still produces positive FCF every year; it does not hit the zero floor. This scenario is what the current price, at the bottom of the 52-week range after a 30% drawdown despite recovering earnings, appears to be discounting.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Hershey is a mature, high-return branded consumer staple whose FY2025 earnings trough was a commodity-cost event, not a franchise event. The valuation is built on a normalised 27% EBITDA margin (FY2022-23 adjusted level, below the FY2024 derivative-boosted peak), mid-single-digit sales growth fading to 2.5%, an owner-FCF basis with SBC and equity-award taxes fully expensed, a flat fully diluted share count of 201.5M, and $4.9B of net debt deducted. Terminal value is capped at 18x terminal FCF in the base case so the model assumes no multiple expansion. The house intrinsic value is the headline; the street value (SBC as non-cash) differs by only a few dollars because SBC is ~0.6% of sales.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cocoa: a return to $10k+/tonne cocoa or cocoa-origin tariffs would push the margin path back toward the FY2025 trough (16.6% EBITDA) rather than the 27% assumed.
Volume: US confectionery category volume has been negative; if GLP-1 and sugar-avoidance trends accelerate, pricing cannot offset it and the bear growth path applies.

Unexplained de-rating: the stock is at its 52-week low after a 30% fall while H1-2026 earnings recovered; if that reflects an FY2026 guidance cut or a new-CEO reset not visible in the Q2-2026 10-Q, the FY2026 drivers are too high.
Tax: the ~11-13% FY2025 effective rate rests on renewable-energy credit investments; a faster run-off than the 17%->20% ramp reduces value ~5%.
Leverage: $5.7B gross debt and a $1.1B dividend leave limited room for a second bad cocoa year; the model deducts net debt but does not model refinancing stress.
Terminal dependence: ~60% of enterprise value is terminal; the 18x cap versus 20x moves the base value by roughly $15/share.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 161.43-239.48.
data_sources.financials: HSY_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL companyfacts, FY2007-Q2 2026); Q2-2026 10-Q (hsy-20260628.htm, filed 2026-07-30) for the cover-page share count, diluted EPS denominator, cash, debt components and operating lease liabilities; FY2025 10-K for SBC, equity-award taxes, cash taxes paid, D&A.
data_sources.qualitative: HSY_Analysis.json was not yet present at build time; narratives draw on the segment description in research/HSY/info.json and the filings' own numbers (cocoa-driven FY2025 margin trough, H1-2026 recovery, LesserEvil, salty snacks).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation add-back $65.46M plus $18.78M cash taxes paid on net-share settlement (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation). Hershey publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases were nil (financing statement). H1-2026 resumed at $439.4M (Q2-2026 10-Q), so the flat share count is being funded, not merely assumed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Cover of the Q2-2026 10-Q: 146,312,143 Common + 54,613,514 Class B = 200.93M at 27 Jul 2026, plus ~0.56M dilutive PSU/RSU/option effect from the Q2-2026 diluted EPS denominator (202.745M diluted vs 202.187M basic). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (expensing and diluting would double-charge).
inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt $5,693.3M per Q2-2026 balance sheet (long-term debt $4,685.0M + current portion $504.2M + short-term borrowings $421.5M = $5,610.7M, remainder is finance-lease/other borrowings in the DB aggregate). Cash and equivalents $791.2M (XBRL CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents, restricted portion immaterial). Operating lease liabilities of $312.6M are NOT added: operating-lease cost sits inside EBITDA under ASC 842, so the flows are already post-lease.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~0.55 for a branded US confectioner with ~13% debt in the capital structure -> cost of equity ~7.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.8% (FY2025 interest expense $225M on ~$5.4B average debt = 4.2%, marked up for the Aug-2025 issuance), after-tax ~3.9%. Weighted ~6.6%, rounded up to 7.0% for commodity (cocoa) earnings volatility that the scenario weights do not fully capture. Same 7.0% in all three scenarios so that risk is charged once, through the weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842) are expensed inside EBITDA; lease liabilities excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest (XBRL MinorityInterest nil since FY2021).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company, consumer'. Hershey is a branded confectionery/snacks manufacturer with a real FCF stream, no deposits, no fair-value-driven earnings, no live corporate action; the owner-FCF engine applies directly. US filer, USD flows and quote, so owner-fcf-adaptations was consulted only for the lease and working-capital rules. FY0 is FY2025, a cocoa-cost trough year: reported EBITDA margin 16.6% versus 25-30% in FY2022-24, net income $883M versus $2,221M. H1-2026 has already recovered to a 26.3% EBITDA margin and $893M net income (vs $287M in H1-2025), so the year-1 margin is anchored to the H1-2026 run-rate rather than the FY2025 trough; the FY2025 owner FCF of $1,738.5M is recorded as last_fcf for auditability but the projection is built from components. Interest income ($34.6M FY2025) is NOT stripped because the company carries $4.9B net debt, not net cash. The price sits at the bottom of its 52-week range (161-239) despite the H1-2026 earnings recovery; the filings alone do not explain that de-rating, so the bear weight is raised above the house default rather than the base path being cut on speculation.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +6% reflects H1-2026 at +8.7% (carry-over pricing, LesserEvil consolidation from Q2-2025) against a tougher H2 comp; thereafter the middle of management's 2-4% long-term sales algorithm, fading to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_note: FY2026 25.5% is below the H1-2026 26.3% because Q4 is seasonally the weakest margin quarter; the 27% mature level equals the FY2022-23 adjusted EBITDA margin (adjusted EBIT ~23-24% + D&A ~3.8%) and sits well below the FY2024 reported 29.9%, which carried derivative mark-to-market gains.
base.capex_note: FY2023-24 capex of 6.9%/5.4% of revenue was the ERP and Reese's/salty-snacks capacity programme; FY2025 fell to 3.9% and management framed ~$425-450M as the post-programme run-rate. 3.8% fading to 3.5%, slightly below D&A.
base.tax_note: FY2025 cash taxes were 13% of pretax profit and management has guided an unusually low ETR (~11-13%) driven by renewable-energy tax-credit investments; H1-2026 cash taxes ran ~19%. Ramp 17% -> 20%: the credits are real but finite, and 20% is below the ~24% statutory blend to reflect their partial persistence.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer with receivables + inventory > payables; growth consumes ~5% of the revenue increase.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 25%: the share price has fallen ~30% from its 52-week high while H1-2026 earnings tripled, which says the market sees a forward risk (cocoa re-inflation, tariffs, GLP-1 volume erosion) that the filings do not yet show; commodity cost exposure is also the one input the company cannot control. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right, full cocoa normalisation and sustained positive US volume, and Hershey's own long-term algorithm is only 2-4% sales growth. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
